answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with proof of patience: a new identity starts at the foot of a knoll, able only to take tiny jobs, and climbs toward trusted work only after many epochs of verified useful activity. Reputation cannot be forged in bulk, each identity ages in real time, and idleness erodes its standing, recorded in a sable-ink ledger no one can rewrite. A farmer spawning ten thousand clones gains ten thousand novices, none trusted, while the cost of aging them all dwarfs any payout.
